intro: Listen for the water. You are at Eflatunpınar Hittite Monument in Konya province, from the 13th century BC. This is a Hittite sacred pool, built over a spring and faced with gods and goddesses: one of the few monumental water structures the Hittites left standing.
history: In the last century of the Hittite Empire, a monumental pool was built over a spring in dressed stone. Now look at its north face. Winged sun discs, gods and goddesses and mountain deities are stacked one above another. The water is thought to have run into the pool through openings beneath the figures.
highlights: As you wander, don't miss the Sacred pool and the Reliefs of gods and goddesses, look up for the Winged sun disc, and find the spring itself.
facts: Did you know? This is the only monumental Hittite pool that still holds water. The monument was built directly over a spring, and the water still runs where it always did: three thousand years on, the pool designed for it is full today. Monumental Hittite waterworks that survive can be counted on one hand, and Eflatunpınar is the most complete of them.
outro: This brings our journey at Eflatunpınar Hittite Monument to an end. Before you go, please leave the stones untouched, keep to the marked paths and carry water with you. Let the spring keep running for those who come after you. Enjoy your visit.
